name: @three-studio/runtime
description: Game runtime: three.js rendering, Rapier physics, script host. Must never import @three-studio/editor.
//sideEffects: Deliberately absent. Both the component registry (core/src/components/index.ts) and the behaviour registry (runtime/src/Engine.ts) are populated by bare `import './x'` statements, and declaring the package side-effect-free tells every bundler it may drop exactly those — a scene then loads with components no one registered.
//build-tsconfig: esbuild discovers the *root* tsconfig.json on its own, and it honours `paths` — which map @three-studio/* onto sibling source. Without pointing it at the build config, whose `paths` are empty, esbuild inlines core and runtime into every bundle instead of leaving them as the dependencies they are.
//peerDependencies: three is a peer and not a dependency: the whole package is built around `three/webgpu`, and a second copy of three in a consumer's tree makes every `instanceof` across the boundary fail. See the README for the bundler alias it also needs.
